definition: A load balancer spreads incoming requests across several instances of a service. It sends each request to a healthy instance, using a rule such as round robin or fewest connections. When an instance fails its health check, the balancer stops sending it work.
details: A layer-4 balancer forwards connections using addresses and ports. A layer-7 balancer can look at the HTTP request and route on the path or host.
examples: Several web servers behind one address
Removing an instance that fails its health check
